items.title:
fr.inria.rules:integraal 3.2.3 发布, InteGraal has been designed in a modular way, in order to facilitate
        software reuse and extension.
        It should make it easy to test new scenarios and techniques, in
        particular by combining algorithms.
        The main features of Graal are currently the following:
        (1) internal storage to store data by using a SQL or RDF representation
        (Postgres, MySQL, HSQL, SQLite, Remote SPARQL endpoints, Local in-memory
        triplestores) as well as a native in-memory representation
        (2) data-integration capabilities for exploiting federated heterogeneous
        data-sources through mappings able to target systems such as SQL, RDF,
        and black-box (e.g. Web-APIs)
        (3) algorithms for query-answering over heterogeneous and federated data
        based on query rewriting and/or forward chaining (or chase)

org.mock-server:mockserver-bom 9.0.0 发布, Bill of Materials for MockServer. Import this BOM into the dependencyManagement section
        of a consuming project to align every MockServer module (mockserver-core, mockserver-netty,
        mockserver-junit-jupiter, the Spring integrations, and the rest) to a single, mutually consistent
        version, so you can declare any MockServer artifact without repeating its version.

        This BOM manages ONLY MockServer's own org.mock-server artifacts. It deliberately does NOT pin the
        third-party libraries MockServer depends on internally (Jackson, Netty, Guava, Nimbus, Velocity,
        SLF4J, …), so importing it never changes the versions — or scopes — your project resolves for those
        shared libraries. Manage third-party versions yourself, or import each upstream project's own BOM.

        via ServiceLoader and runs the Service it creates, without compiling
        against the implementation.

        Carries three things: the ServiceProvider/Service interfaces, the
        manifest a service uses to describe itself, and CliBuilder, which turns
        described parameters into the argument array the provider is created
        with. The manifest and the builder are here because both sides must
        agree on them exactly: a host that derived arguments its own way would
        be a second implementation of the contract, differing from the first
        only where it was wrong.

        No host internals and no implementation of any service. Published
        publicly so providers and hosts share one contract without copying
        source; the implementations stay private and are delivered to hosts as
        runtime plugin jars.
